This production seems intent on appealing to TikTok audiences who don't know much about the play going in, which is a laudable goal, and I think it will succeed.
Unfortunately, the production's rave-like, nihilistic drive does little to make up for its lack of clarity or a pulse.
More often than not, it irks, like an overly enthusiastic theater teacher straining to get equally enthusiastic kids interested in the classics
Although the production has a heartbeat, it's missing a heart.
Such is the enervating effect of so aggressively clickbaity and uncurious a production.
The stellar production succeeds in threading the needle between two nearly impossible tasks.
It's all a very pleasant surprise that this Romeo + Juliet is wildly enjoyable, acutely contemporary, potently acted, and often surprisingly revealing.
The most gorgeous moments in this Romeo + Juliet are the simplest, when all the noise falls away and it's just Connor and Zegler.
Looking back on his Hamlet, Othello, Lear, Macbeth, I'd say Gold has a mixed track record with the major tragedies (watch out, Titus!). This one I'll remember fondly.
Connor, Zegler and a cast that also includes Gabby Beans, Tommy Dorfman, Daniel Bravo Hernndez and others are engaging from beginning to end.
He occasionally achieves something gorgeous and intimate, thanks in large part to the white-hot chemistry of his two leads.
On that end, 'Romeo + Juliet' is a let-down.
Alas, while the two leads are sincere, the show itself is (a) altogether too much of too much; (b) a bit of an ill-focused mess; (c) less than engrossing.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this high-energy, contemporary take: some praise the leads' chemistry and accessibility for young audiences, while others find it an unfocused, gimmicky mess that sacrifices emotional depth for flashy style.
